message.content:
YOUR WORKING DIRECTORY IS `/opt/nxeon-agent-console` — a git worktree (branch agent/console) of the Nxeon shared-hosting platform (Next.js 15 App Router + Prisma). Do ALL work there. NEVER touch /opt/nxeon (live prod) or other /opt/nxeon-* worktrees. `cd /opt/nxeon-agent-console` first. node_modules is symlinked so tsc/build work.

# TASK: Rebuild the customer shared-hosting panel into a proper "console" that matches an approved mockup, with all resources SCOPED INSIDE THE PLAN, and each website drillable into its own isolated page.

## Your spec: the mockup
Open `HOSTING_MOCKUP_REFERENCE.html` in your worktree root (a self-contained clickable prototype). THAT is the target layout and interaction. Study it — the plan console (resource stat-cards + website grid + Activity/Plan/Usage row + right rail) and the website-detail drill-down (click "Manage" on a website → a page scoped to just that site with its own sub-nav). Match its flow and quality; improve where sensible. Use the same dark brand (navy #080b16 ground, violet #8b5cf6 → cyan #22d3ee accents — NO amber). Then DELETE HOSTING_MOCKUP_REFERENCE.html before committing (it's just a reference, must not ship).

## Current state to build ON (don't rebuild the working panels)
The plan console lives at `app/dashboard/hosting/[id]/page.tsx` + `components/customer/hosting/HostingTabs.tsx` (a tabbed layout) and these panels already WORK and must keep working: `WebsitesPanel.tsx`, `FileManager.tsx`, `DatabasesPanel` , `EmailTab.tsx`, `BackupsPanel`, `SubdomainsPanel`/`AddonDomainsPanel` (Domains), `AppInstaller.tsx`, cron, `SettingsTab`, `HostingUpgradePanel.tsx` (storage + plan upgrade), `AppCredentials.tsx`, the Logs tab, `RenameCard`. Recent work already added: plan name (`HostingAccount.name` + `displayName`, `renameHostingAccount`), per-website credential de-dupe, per-domain email, storage/plan upgrades, a website switcher, a Logs tab. Reuse ALL of it. Read `lib/actions-hosting.ts` for the read/mutation actions (`toView`/`HostingAccountView`, `listWebsites`, `listHostingTaskLog`, `getHostingAppCredentials`, databases/email/backup reads, etc.).

## What to build (RESHAPE the shell + navigation; reuse the functional panels as section content)
1. **Plan console = the new default view** (replaces the current Overview/tab-bar feel):
   - Header: plan **displayName** (with rename affordance) + tier chip + Active status; ONE primary CTA "Add Website", plus "Upgrade Plan" / "Upgrade Storage" (no duplicate copies of these buttons elsewhere — see redundancy notes).
   - A row of **resource stat-cards SCOPED TO THIS PLAN**: Websites, Storage, Databases, Emails, Backups — each shows the live count/quota (from the account view) AND is the click-through to that plan-scoped section (the cards ARE the primary navigation).
   - **Website grid** as the hub (from `listWebsites`): each website a card (hostname, Primary/Active badges, app, per-site metrics, "Manage" → website detail, "⋯" menu) + an "Add New Website" card.
   - A bottom row: **Recent Activity** (from `listHostingTaskLog`), **Plan Information** (plan/status/billing/price/next-due — MERGE the old "Plan Details" feature checklist and "Plan Information" into ONE coherent block, they were redundant), and **Resource Usage** ONLY if real data exists (storage/inodes/bandwidth are on the account; CPU/memory may not be — show what's real, drop what isn't rather than faking).
   - A slim right rail is optional — if it adds redundancy, fold its content into the main column. Be sensical.
2. **Plan-scoped resource sections** (Databases, Emails, Backups, SSL/Domains, File Manager, Cron, Logs, Settings): reachable from the stat-cards and/or a secondary in-plan nav. REUSE the existing panels verbatim as the content — just reframe them as sections of this plan's console (URL like `?tab=databases`). Keep them all reachable and working.
3. **Website detail drill-down** (click "Manage" on a website): a view scoped to ONE website with its own sub-nav — Overview, App, Files, Domains & SSL, Email, Databases, Logs, Settings — reusing the existing per-site capabilities (per-site install via `installWordPress(accountId, target)`/`installApp`, the file manager with `initialPath` at that docroot, `listWebsites` per-site data, set-primary for addon domains). Navigable via URL (e.g. `?site=<id>` + a per-site sub-tab). Where a per-site view doesn't have dedicated data yet, reuse the account-level panel filtered/scoped as best you can, or show a clear "managed at plan level" link — don't fake data.
4. **Remove the redundancy** the reference had: one "Upgrade Plan" entry, one "Add Website" primary + the grid add-card (drop it from any quick-actions), merge Plan Details+Plan Information, and don't duplicate resource nav in three places — the stat-cards are the nav.

## HARD REQUIREMENTS (the user explicitly asked that everything WORK before staging)
- Preserve every existing hosting feature + every ownership/security guard. Nothing that works today may break.
- Wire to REAL actions/data — no mock/placeholder data in the shipped UI (the mockup's fake data is only a layout reference).
- `npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json` MUST be clean.
- The FULL production build MUST pass (tsc doesn't catch Next server/client-boundary + "use server" errors — e.g. a sync export in a 'use server' file fails the build). Run it and fix everything:
  `export $(grep -E '^DATABASE_URL=' /opt/nxeon-staging/.env | xargs) && npm run build`  (that DB is safe/read-only-at-build; it's staging). The build must reach "Compiled successfully" AND finish generating pages with exit 0.
- Run `npx tsx --test test/hosting.test.ts` — no NEW failures (the one pre-existing `fpm pool` failure is unrelated and OK).

## Deliverable
Delete the reference HTML, commit to agent/console with a clear message. Do NOT push to origin, do NOT promote/deploy. Report: the new page/component structure + routes, which existing panels you reused vs rewrote, how the website drill-down works, the redundancies you removed, any design decisions you made (the user said to make sensible calls), confirmation that `tsc` + full `npm run build` + hosting tests all pass, and any shared-file edits.

content.thinking:
I'm mapping out the architecture for a console-style interface where the page handles routing through URL parameters. The default view shows a plan console, while passing a `site` parameter drills into a specific website's details with its own sub-navigation controlled by additional query parameters.

I'll create a new `HostingConsole` client component to replace the existing `HostingTabs`, managing the view state (plan vs. site detail) and the current section or site tab. The key is reusing the existing functional panels as content sections while reshaping the navigation shell around them.

For the file structure, I'm thinking `HostingConsole.tsx` as the top-level entry, `PlanConsole.tsx` for the hub with stat cards and website grid, and `WebsiteDetail.tsx` for the drill-down view. The header with CTAs (Add Website, Upgrade Plan, Upgrade Storage) and the plan display name should live in the console itself rather than in page.tsx, and the website detail view will have its own breadcrumb header.

On the data side, the console needs to fetch live counts for the stat cards—websites, storage, databases, emails, and backups—which means calling listWebsites, listHostingDatabases, listHostingBackups, listHostingSubdomains, and getHostingEmailStatus from the client. The account object alone doesn't have these live counts, so I'll need those server action calls to populate the stat cards properly.

For navigation, the Websites card should probably link to a dedicated websites section or tab rather than just scrolling to the grid on the hub, since the hub already displays the website grid. I'm thinking the card could navigate to `?tab=websites` to show a full WebsitesPanel and avoid redundancy.

The other stat cards would each link to their respective sections: Storage goes to the upgrade section, Databases to the databases section, Emails to the email section, and Backups to the backups section. But there are also Domains, Files, Cron, and Logs sections that need to be accessible, so I'll add a secondary navigation row with section tabs or links alongside the stat cards to cover everything.

Actually, I think the cleanest approach is to have a section switcher that's always visible when you're in any section, letting you move between them easily. On the hub itself, the stat cards serve as the primary entry points, and I'll add a compact row like "Manage: Domains · Files · Cron · Logs · Settings" for the sections without stat cards.

Now I need to think through the implementation carefully to avoid breaking anything. I'll set up the page component to fetch the account and pass it to the HostingConsole component, moving the header logic inside. I also need to add a new search parameter for the site sub-tab — I'll call it `stab` — while keeping the existing `site`, `tab`, and `path` parameters. The HostingConsole component will manage state for which site is selected (undefined means showing the plan view), the site tab, and the current section, then render either the plan view or site details accordingly, syncing everything with the URL history.

I'm defining the sections list that includes the hub overview, databases, email, backups, domains, files, cron jobs, logs, and settings. The key insight is that the hub itself displays the websites grid, so there's no need for a separate websites section — this eliminates the conceptual duplication that existed before. When managing a specific website, you navigate into its detail view. I need to handle the existing deep links that reference `?tab=websites&site=<id>`, but since I'm refactoring the openFiles method anyway, I can update those references as part of the migration.

The tension here is that WebsitesPanel is marked as existing functionality that must keep working, yet the task asks me to build a new website grid for the hub using listWebsites. Done. Committed to `agent/console` (not pushed, not deployed). The reference HTML is deleted.

## What I built

Reshaped the customer shared-hosting panel from a flat tab-bar into a plan-as-workspace **console** matching the mockup. All data is wired to the real ownership-guarded server actions — no mock data.

**New structure / routes** (`/opt/nxeon-agent-console`):
- `app/dashboard/hosting/[id]/page.tsx` — thin server page: fetches the account (owner-or-admin guard preserved) and renders the console, passing `tab / path / site / stab` search params.
- `components/customer/hosting/HostingConsole.tsx` (new, ~1000 lines) — the whole shell:
  - **Plan console** (default view): header with **inline rename** (reuses `renameHostingAccount`) + tier chip + status; one `Add Website` / `Upgrade Plan` / `Upgrade Storage` CTA each; a row of **5 plan-scoped stat-cards** (Websites, Storage, Databases, Emails, Backups) with live counts/quotas that ARE the primary nav; a **website grid hub** from `listWebsites` (per-card Manage → detail, `⋯` menu for open-files/visit/set-primary/delete, plus an Add-New-Website card); a bottom row of **Recent Activity** (`listHostingTaskLog`) + **merged Plan card** + **Resource Usage** (renders only when real storage/inode data exists); a slim right rail with the DNS→HTTPS go-live stepper + `recheckHostingHealth`, SFTP reveal, and a support link.
  - **Plan-scoped sections** (`?tab=databases|email|backups|domains|files|cron|logs|settings`): reuse the existing panels verbatim as section content, reachable from the stat-cards and a secondary in-plan nav.
  - **Website detail drill-down** (`?site=<id|primary>&stab=<subtab>`): scoped to one site with its own sub-nav (Overview, App, Files, Domains & SSL, Email, Databases, Logs, Settings) — reuses per-site install (`installWordPress`/`installApp` with `SiteTarget`), `FileManager` at the site's docroot, set-primary and delete. Email/Databases show clear "managed at plan level" links (they aren't per-site) rather than faking data.
